title: Formal compositional inverse identities for logarithm and exponential
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra and $R[[T]]$ its ring of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Define
$$L(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}nT^n,\qquad A(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n!}T^n.$$
For $F(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nT^n$ and $G(T)$ of constant coefficient zero, write $F\circ G=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nG(T)^n$, where each coefficient is a finite sum. Then in $R[[T]]$,
$$L\circ A=T,\qquad A\circ L=T.$$
These are identities of formal series; no topology or convergence assumption is imposed on $R$.
